# Skill Catalog Index

- `canvas2d-animation` — draws expressive hand-drawn / procedural art on a 2D canvas (pen, marker, chalk, brush); reach for it when the scene wants a whiteboard/chalkboard feel, sketched strokes, or particle/procedural texture; skipping risks reaching for SVG or Motion instead gives clean vector geometry that reads as generic, not hand-made.
- `d3-data-visualization` — builds data visualizations and charts (bar, line, pie, scatter, gauge) with D3; reach for it when the scene presents real numeric data, comparisons, or dashboards; skipping risks faking a chart in Motion/SVG yields mis-scaled axes and unreadable data.
- `lottie-animation` — renders precise keyframed vector animations from Lottie/bodymovin JSON; reach for it when the scene needs micro-animations, icon motion, or designer-authored keyframe control; skipping risks approximating Lottie motion in CSS drops the precise easing and motion personality.
- `motion-css-animation` — orchestrates layout-heavy explainers with the anime.js master timeline, text splitting, and DreambyteMotion; reach for it when the scene is text reveals, staggered element entrances, or a typographic explainer beat; skipping risks hand-rolling reveals without the timeline produces uncoordinated, janky staggers.
- `svg-animation` — animates clean vector graphics with CSS/SMIL inside an SVG viewBox; reach for it when the content is simple flat vector shapes that need lightweight, crisp motion; skipping risks using Canvas2D or Three.js over-engineers a flat graphic and loses vector crispness.
- `threejs-3d-scene` — composes immersive 3D scenes with PBR materials, environments, and camera flyovers (Three.js r183); reach for it when the content is genuinely spatial — 3D products, environments, WebGL effects, 3D scatter; skipping risks simulating depth in 2D looks flat; stacking 3D on a 2D idea wastes a heavy renderer.
